subtitle: When a King Turned Time into His Banner

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a royal figure before a massive stone inscription wall
panels.action: Vikramaditya VI stands tall in Kalyani’s palace courtyard, hand outstretched toward an enormous freshly carved stone slab, its surface dense with inscription lines, ministers and scribes frozen behind him in awe.

dialogue.text: In 1076 CE, Vikramaditya VI of Kalyani did something strange and bold: he made his own accession the starting-point of time itself in his realm.

i18n.hi: १०७६ ई में, कल्याणी के विक्रमादित्य षष्ठ ने साहसी काम किया—अपने राज्य में समय की शुरुआत ही अपने गद्दी पर बैठने से तय कर दी।

panels.shot: dramatic mid-shot in a dim palace hall
panels.action: Vikramaditya VI, younger but battle-hardened, strides into a torchlit Kalyani throne hall, Someshvara II’s throne visible at the far end, courtiers turning with tense, uncertain faces.

dialogue.text: The records say that in 1076 CE Vikramaditya VI seized the Kalyani throne from his brother Someshvara II, and the later Chalukyas entered their longest, strongest reign.

i18n.hi: लिखितों में है कि १०७६ ई में विक्रमादित्य षष्ठ ने भाई सोमेश्वर द्वितीय से कल्याणी का सिंहासन छीना, और पश्चिमी चालुक्यों का सबसे लंबा, मजबूत राज शुरू हुआ।

panels.shot: slow push-in close-up on the throne and coronation scene
panels.action: Seated now upon the ornate Chalukya throne, Vikramaditya VI receives a ritual coronation; priests pour water from golden kalashas, while a senior court scribe kneels nearby with palm-leaf bundle and stylus ready.

dialogue.text: Coronation brought the usual titles and praise, but one question hung in the air of Kalyani’s halls: how would this new ruler mark his difference from the kings before him?

i18n.hi: राज्याभिषेक पर ढेरों उपाधियाँ और प्रशंसा मिली, पर कल्याणी के महलों में एक सवाल गूंजता रहा—ये नया राजा खुद को पुराने राजाओं से अलग कैसे दिखाएगा?

panels.shot: intimate close-up of Vikramaditya VI in council chamber
panels.action: In a quieter council chamber, Vikramaditya VI sits in thoughtful profile, palm resting on his chin, as poets, jurists and officers stand in a semicircle; a rolled copperplate grant lies on a low table before them.

dialogue.text: Elsewhere in India, grants were dated in eras like the Saka years. Scribal habit and royal duty moved together. Vikramaditya’s court now weighed how his accession should be remembered in stone.

i18n.hi: भारत के और हिस्सों में दान-पत्रों पर शाका जैसे युग चलते थे—लेखकों की आदत और राजधर्म साथ चलते। अब विक्रमादित्य का दरबार सोच रहा था कि उसकी गद्दीनशीनी पत्थर पर कैसे याद रखी जाए।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot from behind Vikramaditya VI towards assembled scholars
panels.action: From behind Vikramaditya VI, we see a circle of learned men—one poet with a manuscript, one jurist with law treatise—standing respectfully, the flicker of lamps casting long shadows on carved stone pillars.

dialogue.speaker: vikramaditya_vi
dialogue.text: If kings pass and time endures, let my reign itself be the measure of time.

i18n.hi: “राजा आते-जाते हैं, समय रहता है—तो मेरे राज को ही समय की नाप बना दो।”

panels.shot: dramatic close-up on a stone inscription being chiseled
panels.action: A sculptor-scribe chisels fine Nagari and Kannada letters into a tall stone slab; behind him, Vikramaditya VI oversees, pointing with a firm hand to a line where a date formula is being carved.

dialogue.text: In 1076 CE a new formula begins to appear: the Chalukya-Vikrama era. Inscriptions now count years not just from cosmic cycles, but from Vikramaditya’s own accession.

i18n.hi: १०७६ ई के बाद एक नया हिसाब दिखने लगा—चालुक्य-विक्रम युग। अब अभिलेखों में साल सिर्फ ब्रह्मांडीय चक्रों से नहीं, विक्रमादित्य की गद्दीनशीनी से गिने जाने लगे।

panels.shot: tight close-up of inscription lines on stone
panels.action: The camera lingers on incised lines: elegant Sanskrit date phrasing in Nagari script above, neat Kannada lines below, brackets of floral borders framing the words; Vikramaditya VI’s royal titles fill the visible portion.

dialogue.text: The stone speaks: so many years of Chalukya-Vikrama, so many victories, so many grants. The king’s name and era fuse, making his rule the backbone of every recorded day.

i18n.hi: पत्थर बोल उठे—इतने साल चालुक्य-विक्रम, इतनी जीतें, इतने दान। राजा का नाम और युग जुड़कर हर दर्ज दिन की रीढ़ बन गए।

panels.shot: wide shot of temple courtyard with multiple inscriptions
panels.action: In a Gadag temple courtyard, several standing stones and copperplate recipients are being displayed; priests, donors and officials gather, with Vikramaditya VI visiting in procession under a parasol.

dialogue.text: From Kalyani to Gadag and Lakkundi, hundreds of Kannada and Sanskrit inscriptions carry this era. Each grant, each boundary mark, ties land and duty back to Vikramaditya’s chosen starting point.

i18n.hi: कल्याणी से गदग और लक्कुंडी तक, कन्नड़ और संस्कृत के सैकड़ों अभिलेख यही युग रखते हैं। हर दान, हर सरहद की निशानी जमीन और जिम्मा विक्रमादित्य की चुनी हुई शुरुआत से बांध देती है।

panels.shot: mid-shot in a scholarly chamber filled with manuscripts
panels.action: Inside a refined court library, Vikramaditya VI sits among manuscripts; a learned poet, representing Bilhana, recites from a palm-leaf text, while another scholar gestures toward a legal manuscript on a stand.

dialogue.text: Bilhana’s Vikramanka-deva-charita and Vijnaneshwara’s Mitakshara emerge in this same reign. Royal culture, law and poetry now move in step with an era named after the king himself.

i18n.hi: बिल्हण का ‘विक्रमांकदेवचरित’ और विज्नानेश्वर की ‘मिताक्षरा’ भी इसी राज में निकलीं—दरबारी संस्कृति, कानून और कविता अब उसी युग की चाल में चलने लगीं, जिसका नाम खुद राजा पर था।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Vikramaditya VI listening to a jurist
panels.action: Vikramaditya VI leans forward, attentive, as the jurist holds his Mitakshara manuscript open, explaining a point while an inscription stone looms in the background, linking oral discourse to written record.

dialogue.text: The Mitakshara comments on ancient dharma texts, fixing rules of inheritance and duty. The inscriptions fix land and authority in his name. Law in leaves, power in stone, all under one regnal era.

i18n.hi: मिताक्षरा पुराने धर्मग्रंथों पर टीका कर विरासत और कर्तव्य के नियम तय करती है। अभिलेख जमीन और सत्ता उसके नाम पर ठोक देते हैं—पत्तों पर कानून, पत्थर पर ताकत, सब एक ही राज-युग के नीचे।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye wide shot of Deccan landscape dotted with temples
panels.action: A high view over the western Deccan shows scattered temple complexes, village clusters and roads; stylized markers indicate locations like Lakkundi and Vengi, with small inscription stones at key sites.

dialogue.text: This was no pan-Indian reform. Saka years still marked time elsewhere. The Chalukya-Vikrama era was a regional claim, a dynastic stamp on the western Deccan and its connected lands.

i18n.hi: ये कोई पूरे भारत की सुधार नहीं थी—और जगह शाका साल ही चलते रहे। चालुक्य-विक्रम युग एक प्रांतीय दावा था—पश्चिमी दक्कन और उसके जुड़े इलाकों पर वंश की मुहर।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-shot of a scribe writing Kannada on a copperplate
panels.action: A court scribe bends over a shining copperplate, incising Kannada script with care; in the background, Vikramaditya VI and local chiefs discuss, a map spread between them.

dialogue.text: Many records speak in Kannada, some in Sanskrit, some in both. Vernacular language, royal titles and this new era intertwine, showing how power now speaks through local words and precise dates.

i18n.hi: कई लेख कन्नड़ में हैं, कुछ संस्कृत में, कुछ दोनों में—बोली, राजउपाधियाँ और नया युग ऐसे घुलते हैं कि दिखता है अब ताकत स्थानीय शब्दों और सही तारीखों से बोलती है।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Vikramaditya VI inspecting boundary stones in countryside
panels.action: In open countryside, Vikramaditya VI on horseback pauses by freshly set boundary stones inscribed with short date lines; village elders stand nearby, fields stretching toward the horizon.

dialogue.text: A boundary stone dated in Chalukya-Vikrama years tells farmers where one grant ends and another begins. The counting of years now guides the counting of harvests and dues.

i18n.hi: चालुक्य-विक्रम सालों में दिनांकित सरहद का पत्थर किसानों को बताता है कि एक दान कहाँ खत्म और दूसरा कहाँ शुरू—सालों की गिनती अब फसल और लगान की गिनती भी चलाती है।

panels.shot: close-up on Vikramaditya VI’s contemplative face at dusk
panels.action: At dusk on a Kalyani terrace, Vikramaditya VI stands alone, looking over the city as lamps flicker to life; below, silhouettes of inscription stones dot the palace complex.

dialogue.text: Year after year, stones and plates repeat the same framing: so many years since Vikramaditya’s accession. His political moment stretches into a long institutional horizon.

i18n.hi: साल दर साल, पत्थर और ताम्रपट वही ढांचा दोहराते हैं—विक्रमादित्य की गद्दीनशीनी से इतने वर्ष। उसका राजनीतिक पल खिंचकर लंबे संस्थागत क्षितिज में बदल जाता है।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide shot showing passage of time around inscription
panels.action: A single tall inscription stone stands unmoved as seasons shift around it—monsoon clouds, bright sun, pilgrims passing—its carved date formula still crisp despite the weathering.

dialogue.text: After his fifty-year reign ends, dynastic fortunes change, borders shift, kings fall. Yet the era he named survives on surviving stones, a durable habit lodged in epigraphic memory.

i18n.hi: उसके पचास साल के राज के बाद वंश की किस्मतें पलटती हैं, सीमाएँ बदलती हैं, राजा गिरते हैं—पर उसका रखा युग बची हुई शिलालेखों पर चलता रहता है, लेखन की याद में जड़ा हुआ अभ्यास।

panels.shot: archival-feel close-up of modern scholar examining rubbing of inscription
panels.action: In a modern archive setting, a scholar’s hands hold an inscription rubbing; in faint overlay we imagine Vikramaditya VI’s figure, as if watching across time, while the rubbing’s date lines stand out dark.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, historians read these dates to rebuild his story. The Chalukya-Vikrama era turns ambition into evidence, showing how one king made his rule the frame for remembering.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद इतिहासकार इन्हीं तारीखों से उसका किस्सा जोड़ते हैं—चालुक्य-विक्रम युग महत्त्वाकांक्षा को सबूत में बदल देता है, दिखाता है कैसे एक राजा ने अपने राज को याद रखने का ढाँचा बना दिया।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of a corridor lined with inscriptions
panels.action: A long stone corridor is lined with inscriptions from different reigns, but several bear the Chalukya-Vikrama formula; at the far end, a dignified vision of Vikramaditya VI stands in half-shadow, almost fading into stone.

dialogue.text: Vikramaditya VI did not discover a new sky; he fixed a new institution. His era reminds us that power endures most when it teaches others to measure their lives by its rhythm.

i18n.hi: विक्रमादित्य षष्ठ ने कोई नया आसमान नहीं खोजा, उसने नया संस्थान गढ़ा—उसका युग याद दिलाता है कि सत्ता सबसे ज़्यादा तब टिकती है जब वो दूसरों को अपनी धुन पर अपनी ज़िंदगी नापना सिखा दे।

subtitle_i18n.en: When a King Turned Time into His Banner
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब एक राजा ने समय को अपना ध्वज बना लिया
